data.title: Invoicing: AS-38 review follow-ups (T1 tautology, stale health test name, ';' body separator, /healthz config exposure)

data.to:
Four non-blocking findings from the AS-38 QA review (qa-priya, review comment 2026-09-02T00:45Z; items B.4-B.7), bundled because each is a one-line-to-one-function change in apps/invoicing and none changes behaviour visible to a user. AS-38 merged at 66b9fb9.

1. test/stripe-client.test.js:625 — T1 carries a tautological assertion: `!(x in h) || h[x] !== undefined` is always true, so it pins nothing. Either pin the intended property (`'user-agent' not in unsigned.headers` — the transport sends no User-Agent of its own) or delete the line. Decide which the test MEANT; do not just make it pass.

2. test/health.test.js:61 — test name 'no secrets exist yet, so redacted() equals the config' is stale wording since AS-38 introduced the first secret-shaped setting (INVOICING_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY). The assertion still holds because the key is unset in tests. Rename to say what it now checks (an unconfigured secret redacts to null and the rest of the config is unchanged). Flagged independently by both the implementer and the reviewer.

3. lib/stripe/custody.js — guard hardening: a raw `;`-separated body (`customer=cus_1;transfer_data[destination]=acct_x`) passes guardRequest because URLSearchParams splits only on `&`. Unreachable in v1: encodeForm percent-encodes `;` and only client.js may import transport.js (dependency-policy M5b). Fix options, pick one and add the test that fails without it: reject a raw `;` in any body the guard sees, or split on the same separator set Stripe accepts. Keep "values are never inspected" (plan §2).

4. lib/health.js / routes/health.js — /healthz publishes the redacted config object (pre-existing AS-37 behaviour, not an AS-38 criterion). Redaction is proven (AS-38 AC 4, test/health.test.js 'the health body carries redacted config, never raw config'), but a public health endpoint that enumerates setting names and non-secret values (bind, port, env) is more than a health check needs. Decide: drop the config object from /healthz, or gate it behind INVOICING_ENV !== 'production'. Must land before anything is publicly reachable; not urgent while the app runs on loopback only.

Acceptance: each item has a test that fails without the change (house technique — show the checker red once, record the failing-test set); the suite stays 8 files; dependency-policy, deploy-shape and harness guards stay green; no new dependencies; no protected top-level files touched. Complexity low. Plan can be short.

data.body: Filed from Priya's AS-38 review (findings B.4–B.7). Bundled: four one-liners in apps/invoicing, none user-visible. Item 4 (/healthz config exposure) is the only one with a deadline — before anything is publicly reachable.

Implemented on feat/AS-58-as38-review-followups @ 344ddf2 (.worktrees/AS-58). One commit, 8 files in apps/invoicing, no new files, no dependency change.

Item 1 (T1 tautology): deleted. What it MEANT — the client sets no User-Agent — is unobservable at T1: the runtime's fetch puts 'user-agent: node' on the wire regardless (verified). The property is pinned where it is observable, the exact signed-header set in 'client: the transport receives exactly the guarded request plus authorization'; T1 carries a comment saying so.
Item 2: the stale message becomes a test named 'an unconfigured secret redacts to null and the rest of the config is unchanged' — asserts the schema has secret rows (stripeSecretKey, webhookSecret), both null on both sides, redacted() deep-equal to the config.
Item 3: chose SPLIT — checkParams now treats ';' as a pair separator alongside '&', in the body and the query (same hole). Keys-only, no new refusal code, fails closed whichever separator set Stripe honours; encodeForm percent-encodes ';' so no client-built request changes outcome. New test: 40 refusals (10 names × 3 body placements + query), encoded ';' still passes.
Item 4: chose DROP, unconditional — /healthz body is exactly { ok, checks }. Not the env gate: it is only as good as NODE_ENV being right on the public box, which is the class of deploy mistake /healthz exists to catch. Operator signal stays on the startup line. README § Receiving webhooks, config.js/webhooks.js/config.test.js comments updated.

Receipts (scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/AS-58/, mutant-table.md): green 'Image asc-impl-as58-green-test Built', 534/515/0/19 (+2 vs AS-57's 532). Mutants, all with --build receipts and restored=true: F1 red set 1 (the client-level header pin; T1 stayed green, as intended); F2 red set 3 (the renamed test + the two config.test.js null-case rows); F3 red set 1 (the new custody test); F4 red set 1 (the new /healthz-shape test). Observed = predicted on all four. No asc-impl-as58-* leftovers.

Deviations: the description's '8 files' is 23 today (unchanged by this task); plan corrected from a miscounted 24 (ba9ff3d). Description says INVOICING_ENV; the setting is NODE_ENV — moot under the drop. Nothing undone.

Plan and diff read cold; implementer's comment read LAST — independent agreement on all four red sets.

FINDINGS — 4 outside the list, 0 behaviour defects.

1. Stale wording, in the plan's own scope, missed: lib/config.js:14 still says "redacted from every log line and health body". Proposed: drop "and health body". Convention.

2. Guard contract narrowed: a non-string body went from a typed refusal to "TypeError: text.replace is not a function". Measured both trees — master refuses a record object, array-of-pairs and URLSearchParams; 344ddf2 throws. Unreachable (buildUnsigned always passes encodeForm output); fails closed, without a custody code. A String(body) fix fails OPEN: {transfer_data:'x'} becomes "[object Object]", one key, no banned segment.

3. Residual, outside the criteria and scoped out by the plan: a 503 /healthz still publishes path setting values unauthenticated ("/app/vendor/tokens.css: ENOENT", likewise viewsDir and dbPath), so item 4's motive is only partly discharged before the endpoint goes public.

4. The new /healthz needles are key-shaped ('"bind":'), weaker than the criterion's "no setting name in the body text". All 5 reachable states driven: keys exactly [ok,checks], no setting or env-var name — true today, but a future bare name in a detail would pass.

SWEEP — floor check, 5 of 5 met. Red sets all exact: F1 1 (client header pin; T1 green), F2 3, F3 1, F4 1. 534/515/0/19 with receipt; contract 534/534/0/0; 23 test files; lock untouched; four guards green. 24 extra custody probes: 8 refused at the right key/segment, 3 correct pass-throughs, no regex state across calls. Seam: master 8f40cd4 merges clean, suite identical, demo transcript unchanged modulo port/HMAC/UUIDs.

Outcome, since the loop needs one: PASS. Nothing fixed inline; Finding 1 left to the orchestrator. Findings 2-4 are residuals for this record, not new tasks.

Mutant procedure, probe logs, receipts and teardown: scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-58/battery.md
